title: Can a local mean-field predict which robot blocks tip a ring crowd's passing-side convention?
lede: A deterministic local mean-field agrees with the society-allies simulation on tip/no-tip in 145 of 160 cells and is almost never too optimistic, but it overstates the share of evenly spread robots needed (0.20 against 0.12 at k = 2).
summary: A fixed-point map for the ring walking-side game (one number per person, memory slots as independent draws, N = 200, M = 9, ε = 0.02) is compared with the society-allies simulation over 160 cells (robot share 0.04–0.40, blocks 1/2/4/8, neighbourhood k = 1/2/3/5, 10 seeds). It matches the simulated tip/no-tip outcome in 145 cells; in 14 of the other 15 the simulation tips and the map does not. It reproduces the rise of the threshold with block size and its fall with k, within one 0.04 grid step for blocks of 4 and 8 in all 6 such cells at k ≥ 2, but puts the spread-robot threshold at 0.20 against 0.12 simulated. Limits: stylised 1D binary game with chosen M and ε; the cause of the gap (finite-size noise or the memory-independence step) is not tested; thresholds are coarse (±0.04).
